answer: A practical defense is to price identity through ongoing, verifiable work instead of one-time registration. A zephyr of fresh accounts costs almost nothing, but an agent that must keep proving useful behavior over time cannot fake history at scale. Require each agent to stake a small deposit that only unlocks after peers attest its work, like a comet leaving a visible trail: a thousand fresh identities burn out with no trail, while genuine agents build one. A gale of fake accounts then hits a wall, because making each one look real costs as much as being real.
